From: Kathleen O'Gorman <kathogorman@ameritech.net>
Sent: Tuesday, June 5, 2018 12:21 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: Past tense of "sink" 
 
Hi, Anthony,
I'm a former Freep editor. Reading your story today on Casey Mize, I was stopped by the use of "sunk" in the sentence below.
When he sunk into a plush chair in the Auburn athletics auditorium on Monday night ...

The past tense of "sink" is "sank. "Sunk" is the past participle, used with the auxiliary verb "have." I am seeing and even hearing "sunk" used for "sink" more and more often, so you are not alone. Your editor or copy editor should have caught it, but we all make mistakes.
